$schema_note: Machine-readable project state. Source of truth for design; CLAUDE.md is the human-readable view of the same content. When the two disagree, fix one to match the other — don't let drift accumulate.

project.name: reddit_research
project.purpose: Personal Reddit research tool. Single user (Eli's developer account). The use case is: search subreddits for important / useful information for an LLM to summarize.
project.status: design v3 + Phase 0 spike v2 written. Reddit API access request SUBMITTED 2026-04-27 via support form (required by Responsible Builder Policy as of Nov 2025 — self-service script-app creation no longer available). Awaiting Reddit's review (target 7 days, often longer). Spike cannot run until credentials are issued.

decisions.rationale: Matches existing portfolio on the deploy host.
Handles auth, rate-limit backoff, listing pagination, MoreComments expansion. Drop to raw requests against oauth.reddit.com only for endpoints PRAW lacks.

decisions.choice: check_for_updates=False, read_only=True when write flag off
decisions.rationale: Skip per-invocation PyPI call. Defense-in-depth on writes — PRAW refuses write attempts at client level.

decisions.choice: SQLite single file, WAL, busy_timeout=5000, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL
decisions.rationale: Same operational pattern as collector/warehouse on the deploy host. Handles CLI-vs-MCP contention.

decisions.choice: script app + password grant for MVP
decisions.rationale: Existing dev app already works this way. Refresh-token is a security upgrade, not a precondition. Re-evaluate if Reddit deprecates script-app/password-grant policy.

decisions.choice: PEP 621 pyproject.toml, src/ layout, pip install -e . for dev
decisions.rationale: Modern standard. Required for CLI entry point and future MCP server import.

decisions.choice: stdio only, accessed remotely via SSH
decisions.rationale: Eliminates network listener attack surface. Remote access via 'ssh warehouse reddit-mcp'.
CLI provides cheap debug + personal-use surface. MCP is thin glue on top once core is proven.

decisions.choice: cache by default (opt-out), fresh=True per-call to bypass
decisions.rationale: LLM shouldn't have to think about caching ergonomics. Fast-by-default is the point.

decisions.choice: three flat TTLs, no age-aware computation
decisions.rationale: Variable age-aware TTL was overengineered for the 'don't need data for long' research workflow. Add age-awareness later if it proves valuable.

decisions.choice: normalized PRAW objects serialized to JSON dict (NOT byte-for-byte raw)
decisions.rationale: PRAW returns hydrated objects, not raw payloads. Matches actual data flow.

decisions.choice: cache key includes all retrieval params + normalization_version suffix
decisions.rationale: Without this, get_thread(top=20) cache-poisons get_thread(top=100). Discovered in second panel review.
Permanent vs transient. Caching 5xx would poison after one Reddit blip.

decisions.choice: validate ^t[1-6]_[a-z0-9]+$ in core, not at MCP boundary
decisions.rationale: CLI gets the same protection as MCP. Cheap.

decisions.choice: trust PRAW's internal backoff; expose auth.limits via status command
decisions.rationale: Per-call header logging was overkill — PRAW handles backoff correctly. status command is enough for operator visibility.

operations.name: search
operations.signature: search(query, subreddit=None, sort='relevance', time='all', limit=25, fresh=False)
operations.returns: list[ThreadSummary] (title, score, author, sub, num_comments, permalink, fullname, created_utc)

operations.name: get_thread
operations.returns: Thread (post + top N top-level comments by score, no sub-tree expansion)
operations.notes: Cheap by design. LLM picks promising top-level comments to follow up on.

operations.name: expand_comment
operations.returns: CommentTree (one comment + N levels of replies)
operations.notes: The 'follow promising sub-trees' operation. Aggregate per-workflow budget also applies.

operations.name: status
operations.notes: auth_state is one of: never_exercised, last_call_ok, last_call_failed:<reason> — distinguishes bad credentials from 'we just haven't called yet'.

columns.name: cache_key
columns.notes: includes all retrieval params + normalization_version (e.g. ':v1' suffix)

columns.name: body_json
columns.notes: normalized PRAW object dict, or error metadata for non-200

ttl_table.notes: Only 403/404 are cached as errors. 5xx and network errors are never cached.

per_workflow_aggregate_budget.scope: per-process for CLI; per-session for MCP

security.secrets_at_rest: .env mode 0600, cache dir mode 0700, owned by deploy user only
security.mcp_network_exposure: none — stdio only, remote access via SSH
security.write_safety: write flag default off, checked at call time. PRAW read_only=True when flag is off (defense in depth). Audit log of writes is post-MVP.
security.cross_context_isolation: personal vs Motroco data: hard isolation by deployment. Separate service users, separate cache.db, separate credentials per use context. Enforced by Unix file permissions. See historian's personal/CLAUDE.md.

deferred_to_v0_2_or_later: preprocessed views (markdown transforms for token savings)
non_goals: Public exposure of the MCP server
Sharing data between personal and Motroco contexts

phase_0_checklist.task: Auth check: confirm dev app authenticates + pulls one thread via PRAW
Map error behavior: banned/private/deleted thread, observe prawcore exceptions, distinguish 403/404 from 5xx
Verify replace_more(limit=10) on a real big thread
Benchmark queries — 3-5 realistic queries with per-path measurement, real tokenizer counts, signal-to-noise ratio. Save as phase0_benchmarks.md + phase0_benchmarks.json
Cache-hit/miss instrumentation in smoke test for baseline

blockers: Reddit script-app type can't do refresh-token flow (Opus)
Byte-for-byte raw cache is incompatible with PRAW (Codex)
panel_reviews.blockers_resolution: v2: dropped refresh-token requirement (script+password grant fine for personal/single-user); dropped per-call header observability (trust PRAW backoff, expose auth.limits via status); renamed 'raw cache' to 'normalized PRAW objects'.

blockers: Partial-view cache keys must include retrieval params (Codex + Opus, P1) — get_thread(top=20) silently cache-poisons get_thread(top=100)
panel_reviews.blockers_resolution: v3: cache keys now include all retrieval params + normalization_version (':v1' suffix).
should_fix_applied: Per-call caps on expand_comment (depth ≤ 5, limit ≤ 50) + per-workflow aggregate budget
PRAW read_only=True when write flag off
status() distinguishes auth never_exercised from last_call_ok/failed
Phase 0 benchmarks: real tokenizer counts + per-path + signal-to-noise ratio
Validate fullname in core not just MCP boundary

session_log.outcome: Established: full Reddit API surface, read-first for research, write gated. Standalone CLI first; MCP + agents later. Caching opt-in initially.
Hard requirement: don't lose API access. Treat rate budget as ceiling. Mandatory UA discipline.
Scraped reddit.com/dev/api into docs/reddit-api-inventory.json: 19 sections, 202 endpoints, 28 OAuth scopes. Read scope alone covers 44 endpoints — enough for the research path.
Confirmed running on warehouse-vm. Deploy under dedicated service user (suggested: redditmcp). Cache + .env under /home/<deploy>/reddit-cache/.
Two-layer cache (raw + preprocessed); preprocessed layer deferred to v0.2. Variable TTL by kind (later simplified to flat 3 TTLs). fresh=True per-call escape hatch.
Eli wanted optional snapshot capability for delta-over-time research; later confirmed no current use case. Cut from doc; keep architectural room to add later.
3 blockers found, all resolved in v2 by simplification (script+password grant kept, headroom observability dropped, raw renamed to normalized).
Added expand_comment as first-class operation. LLM workflow: search → get_thread (cheap, top-N) → expand_comment on promising sub-trees. Saves API calls + tokens.
1 P1 (cache key bug from adaptive retrieval) + ~10 should-fixes. All applied in v3.
Project added to motroco-document under new personal/ section (parallel to projects/). Hard data-isolation rule established between personal tools and Motroco projects.

Username = joeblowfromidaho. Deploy user = redditmcp (needs creation). Credentials = two .env files (prod at /home/redditmcp/reddit-cache/.env, dev at /home/elib/code/reddit_api/.env) loaded via python-dotenv. Created .env.example (committed) and .gitignore. Phase 0 unblocked — only remaining setup is Eli filling actual credential values into the dev .env.

Created phase0_spike.py + requirements-phase0.txt. Runs 4 probes (auth / errors / morechildren / benchmarks). Each benchmark query measures two paths (list_only and list_plus_threads_top20) with signal-to-noise ratio + token counts via tiktoken cl100k_base. Outputs phase0_notes.md, phase0_benchmarks.md, phase0_benchmarks.json (all gitignored). Ready to run.

3-model panel found 3 P1 issues + 5 P2: full_payload_size included _reddit back-reference (SNR meaningless), more_comments probe used AskReddit top-all-time (rate-budget unsafe), Path 3 (expand_comment) missing per CLAUDE.md spec, missing read_only=True/timeout=30 on PRAW init, comments.list() flattened the tree (wrong shape vs v0.1 get_thread). All applied: filter underscore-prefixed keys in full_payload_size; pick a 200-3000 comment thread from r/python top/month with replace_more(limit=2); added Path 3 (list+threads+expand_one with marginal-cost framing); read_only=True + timeout=30 on PRAW init (auth probe restructured since user.me() returns None in read_only mode); use s.comments (top-level only) not s.comments.list(); honest tokenizer divergence note (5-15%, up to 20% on code-heavy); documented Path 2/3 first-3 sampling bias.

session_log.topic: Reddit API gated by Responsible Builder Policy
session_log.outcome: Discovered self-service script-app registration was killed in Nov 2025; all new OAuth apps now require manual pre-approval via support form. Field reports indicate low approval rates for personal/hobby use cases. Decided to (a) submit anyway with personal-research framing (medical info for wife angle), (b) publish source repo at github.com/elib100/joeblow-research for transparency, (c) plan Reddit .json public endpoint as fallback if rejected.

Panel blocked: 1 P1 (Path 3 measures pre-loaded data because s.comments.replace_more(limit=0) recurses through full tree, leaving nothing for candidate.replies.replace_more to expand — fix: re-fetch submission fresh in Path 3) + 2 P2 (auth contract: with read_only=True, username/password are inert, decide whether to drop from REQUIRED_ENV; SNR shape mismatch in Paths 2/3: full_payload_size on top-level comment includes its already-loaded replies subtree but signal excludes nested replies). Fixes deferred until Reddit access granted (no point iterating without ability to test).
